summary: Cricket and Bollywood controversies remain the top performers, especially when they focus on specific individual records or heated celebrity reactions. Videos that fail often lack a clear, high-energy hook or focus on dry financial or automotive topics that don't connect with the casual viewer. To scale toward monetization, we will pivot to 'reaction-style' cricket news and emotional storytelling around Bollywood star dynamics while ditching slow, informational news segments.
do_more: Focus on 'conflict' or 'record-breaking' news pieces featuring one major Indian celebrity
Use high-contrast thumbnails or visual cues that feature a recognizable star
Ensure every script starts with a 3-second 'pattern interrupt' hook (e.g., 'Ye kaise hua?')
Include a 'call to action' at the end that encourages a sub based on future match or movie predictions
Stick to 40-45 seconds max to keep audience retention and loop-ability high
avoid: Economic news, car specs, or stock market updates that feel too academic
Ambiguous titles that do not name the celebrity or the specific event
Long-winded introductions that don't get straight to the 'why' of the video
Niche international sports updates that lack a connection to an Indian fan-favorite player
hook_tips: Virat Kohli ka ye record todna namumkin kyun hai? Jaan ke hairaan ho jaoge!
Kya Shah Rukh Khan ki nayi film flop hone wali hai? Ye dekho asal sach!
Rohit Sharma ka ye gussa match palat sakta hai! Dekhiye kyun?
Sirf 10 second mein samjho kyun Dhoni ka ye decision sabse bada tha!
title_tips: Use ALL CAPS for the main event (e.g., ROHIT SHARMA RECORD BREAKER!)
Add emojis to stand out in the Shorts feed (🏏, 😱, 🎬, 📈)
Always include a question mark if predicting a result or reacting to a rumor
Keep titles under 50 characters to avoid being cut off on mobile devices
